Update a gcTMB fit, or set its parameters

Source: R/update.R
update.gcTMB.Rd

With fixef, VarCorr, sigma or rho, update returns the model with some of its parameters set to new values, e.g. as the true model of a simulation study (see simulate.gcTMB); the model is not refitted. Without them, it refits the model with the arguments in ... changed, as update.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gcTMB'
update(object, ..., fixef = NULL, VarCorr = NULL, sigma = NULL, rho = NULL)

Arguments

object

A gcTMB object, the result of gcTMB.

...

Without fixef, VarCorr, sigma and rho: the arguments of gcTMB to change, as in update.

fixef

Named numeric vector or NULL. New values of coefficients of b1-b5, named as in fixef (e.g. "b1:(Intercept)"), or by the parameter (e.g. "b1") for a parameter with a single coefficient. Coefficients fixed in the fit, such as the asymmetry b5 (1 by default), can be set too, e.g. fixef=c(b5=4); they stay fixed.

VarCorr

List or NULL. New covariance matrices of the random effects, named by the terms as in VarCorr, with the rows and columns in the same order; a single matrix for a model with one random effect term. The terms that are not given keep their covariance matrices.

sigma

Numeric or NULL. The new residual standard deviation (gaussian, of log(y) for lognormal), or the dispersion parameter of the other families, as returned by sigma.gcTMB.

rho

Numeric or NULL. The new autocorrelation rho of the residuals, as returned by corpars, for a model fitted with a correlation structure: between 0 and 1 for corCAR1, between -1 and 1 for corAR1.

Value

A gcTMB object.

Details

Every parameter of the model can be set: the coefficients of b1-b5 (fixef, including coefficients fixed in the fit), the covariance matrices of the random effects (VarCorr), the residual standard deviation or dispersion (sigma) and the autocorrelation (rho), i.e. all the entries of coef. The parameters that are not given keep their values, and the random effects are the conditional modes at the new parameters. The new values are not estimates: the standard errors, the covariance matrix of vcov and the confidence intervals are NA, and converged returns NA. The log-likelihood is that of the data at the new parameters. To fit the data as well as possible with a chosen value of a parameter, refit the model with that parameter fixed instead, e.g. correlation=corCAR1(0.8, form=~ day | plant, fixed=TRUE) for the autocorrelation, or start=c(b5=2) for the asymmetry, which is fixed by default; the other parameters are then estimated given it, whereas update keeps their values. For gaussian models without random effects, the residual standard deviation is the value given, without the small-sample correction of gcTMB.

Examples

fit <- gcTMB(height ~ DAS, rform=b1 + b2 ~ 1 | plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25)
# larger asymptote, an asymmetric curve, and a larger variance of b1
vc <- VarCorr(fit)$plant_ID
vc[1, 1] <- 2*vc[1, 1]
fit2 <- update(fit, fixef=c(b1=150, b5=4), VarCorr=list(plant_ID=vc))
fixef(fit2)
#> b1:(Intercept) b2:(Intercept) b3:(Intercept) b5:(Intercept) 
#>      150.00000       30.86626       12.84146        4.00000 
VarCorr(fit2)
#> $plant_ID
#>            b1        b2
#> b1 209.588060 -3.159913
#> b2  -3.159913  6.558684
#> attr(,"stddev")
#>        b1        b2 
#> 14.477156  2.560993 
#> attr(,"correlation")
#>             b1          b2
#> b1  1.00000000 -0.08522823
#> b2 -0.08522823  1.00000000
#> 
#> attr(,"sc")
#> [1] 2.074042
# refit with another growth model
fitg <- update(fit, model="gompertz")
# a weaker autocorrelation of the residuals, the other parameters unchanged
fitc <- gcTMB(height ~ DAS, rform=b1 ~ 1 | plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25,
              correlation=corCAR1(form=~ DAS | plant_ID))
corpars(update(fitc, rho=0.7))
#> rho 
#> 0.7
